questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

The diagram shows the private and social costs and benefits of production in a free market that result in market failure. MSC costs, benefits MPC MSB MPB O K L M N output Which change in output would be necessary to overcome this market failure?

options.A: from K to M
options.B: from M to N
options.C: from M to L

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the production possibility curve for an economy. good Y L O good X What might make it possible for consumers in this economy to consume the combination of goods X and Y indicated by the point L?

options.A: a reduction in unemployment
options.B: the achievement of productive efficiency
options.C: the elimination of a monopoly in the production of good X

questions.questionText: The diagram shows two indifference curves for a consumer. good Y R Q IC IC O good X What can be concluded if the consumer’s equilibrium moves from Q to R?

options.A: The consumer is acting rationally.
options.B: The consumer’s money income is unchanged.
options.C: The opportunity cost of good Y is constant.
options.D: The price of good X has risen.

questions.questionText: When the price of a good falls the effect on the quantity demanded is the result of an income effect and a substitution effect. Which statement about these effects is correct?

options.A: For inferior goods the income effect and the substitution effect work in the same direction.
options.B: For inferior, but not Giffen, goods the income effect outweighs the substitution effect.
options.C: For normal goods the income effect and substitution effect work in the same direction.
options.D: For normal goods the income effect outweighs the substitution effect.

questions.questionText: Where is the long-run equilibrium output of a perfectly competitive firm?

options.A: where average costs are at a minimum
options.B: where average costs are falling
options.C: where marginal costs are at a minimum

questions.questionText: A firm estimates that, all else remaining unchanged, an increase in its output will result in an equal proportionate increase in its revenue. What can be concluded from this?

options.A: The demand curve for the firm’s product is horizontal.
options.B: The firm operates in a monopolistically competitive market.
options.C: The price elasticity of demand for the firm’s product is –1.
options.D: The supply of the firm’s product is perfectly inelastic.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s cost and revenue curves. cost, revenue MC AC MR AR O output The firm changes its objective from profit maximisation to sales revenue maximisation. Which groups are likely to be winners and losers as a result of this change? winners losers

options.A: customers shareholders
options.B: managers customers
options.C: workers managers

questions.questionText: What could be a reason for the existence of small firms in various industries?

options.A: a low minimum efficient scale of production
options.B: greater scope for specialisation and division of labour
options.C: the need to diversify in order to reduce risk

questions.questionText: A firm in monopolistic competition that is producing at its profit maximising output is making a loss in the short run. For it to continue in production, what must be correct about its average revenue (AR), marginal revenue (MR) and average variable cost (AVC)?

options.A: AR = MR; AVC > AR
options.B: AR = MR; AVC < AR
options.C: AR > MR; AVC > AR

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve for a firm’s product. price O output Which diagram shows the shape of the firm’s total revenue (TR) curve?

options.A: B C D revenue revenue revenue revenue O O O O output output output output

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm in monopoly producing OQ units. MC ATC price $ AVC MR D O Q quantity Which outcome can be observed in the diagram?

options.A: loss minimisation
options.B: profit satisficing
options.C: revenue maximisation

questions.questionText: Which feature of oligopoly is being assumed when the demand curve for an individual firm is as shown? price D D O quantity

options.A: price discrimination
options.B: price leadership by the dominant firm
options.C: interdependence between firms

questions.questionText: Which statement is most likely to explain why a government decides to increase the highest rates of tax on personal income?

options.A: It expects total tax revenue to be unaffected by the policy change.
options.B: It is concerned about the possibility of emigration by some high earning individuals.
options.C: It regards equity considerations as being more important than efficiency ones.
options.D: It wishes to switch the emphasis of its tax system from direct to indirect taxation.

questions.questionText: The Lorenz curves in the diagram show different distributions of income and of wealth. % of income or % of wealth 0 100 % of households Income in a country is more equally distributed than wealth. In a period the distribution of income becomes more unequal but the distribution of wealth becomes more equal. Which movement would show the effects of these changes on the distribution of income and wealth within the country? distribution of income distribution of wealth

options.A: shift from curve 1 to curve 2 shift from curve 4 to curve 3
options.B: shift from curve 2 to curve 1 shift from curve 3 to curve 4
options.C: shift from curve 3 to curve 4 shift from curve 2 to curve 1
options.D: shift from curve 4 to curve 3 shift from curve 1 to curve 2

questions.questionText: A government wishes to discourage tax avoidance. Which policy to achieve this would be an example of the behavioural approach of nudge theory?

options.A: compelling direct tax deduction by employers
options.B: making random inspections of individual tax records
options.C: providing information on how the tax is spent by the government
options.D: using penalties, such as fines and imprisonment for tax avoidance

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the supply and demand situation in a particular labour market. supply wage rate N L M J demand O K quantity of labour When the market is in equilibrium, which areas measure the economic rent and transfer earnings received by employees? economic rent transfer earnings

options.A: JLN OKLJ
options.B: JML OKLJ
options.C: NML OKLM

questions.questionText: In 2015 a company drilling for oil wished to reduce its workforce because of a fall in the price of oil. The workers’ trade union opposed the proposal. Which situation would have helped the trade union in the negotiations?

options.A: Capital and labour were close substitutes.
options.B: The cost of labour had been a small percentage of total cost.
options.C: The demand for oil had been price inelastic.
options.D: There had been a large supply of labour.

questions.questionText: Which policy is specifically designed to reduce the level of structural unemployment?

options.A: an increase in the level of state benefits paid to the unemployed
options.B: a reduction in interest rates
options.C: a reduction in the level of direct taxation

questions.questionText: What is typically associated with a relatively low level of income per capita in a country?

options.A: low exports
options.B: low inflation
options.C: low investment

questions.questionText: During a certain period, a country with a constant population expands its output per head. It also experiences a significant increase in river and atmospheric pollution. In the absence of any other changes, which measure would show a decrease in living standards?

options.A: Gross Domestic Product per head
options.B: Gross National Product per head
options.C: Human Development Index

questions.questionText: The graphs below show percentage changes in money GDP and consumer prices in a country between 2008 and 2010. % % 2008 2009 2010 2008 2009 2010 % change in % change in money GDP consumer prices Which conclusion may be drawn from the graphs?

options.A: Between 2009 and 2010 money GDP fell but consumer prices continued to rise.
options.B: Consumer prices and money GDP both continued to rise throughout the period.
options.C: In real terms GDP grew throughout the period.
options.D: When consumer prices rose, money GDP fell.

questions.questionText: Why do some economists suggest there may be positive benefits from frictional unemployment?

options.A: A short spell of frictional unemployment may lead workers to become discouraged.
options.B: Frictional unemployment allows time for retraining in newly emerging skills.
options.C: Job search during frictional unemployment may lead to a better match of workers and jobs.
options.D: The psychological effects of frictional unemployment are less than the economic effects.

questions.questionText: The table shows the levels of consumption expenditure for given family incomes. disposable consumption family income expenditure ($) ($) 2000 2150 3000 3100 4000 4000 5000 4850 6000 5650 7000 6380 Over the range of disposable income shown, as income rises what happens to the marginal propensity to consume?

options.A: It falls and then rises.
options.B: It falls continuously.
options.C: It rises and then falls.

questions.questionText: Which could cause the official statistics for the national income per head of a developing country to overstate the true level of economic well-being of its inhabitants?

options.A: if there is dependence on barter in internal trade
options.B: if subsistence agriculture dominates total economic activity
options.C: if services are an important component of exports
options.D: if there is extreme income inequality

questions.questionText: The table shows some United Nations population statistics for 2010 and estimates for 2050. total total urban urban population population types of region population population population population urbanised urbanised (m) 2010 (m) 2050 (m) 2010 (m) 2050 (%) 2010 (%) 2050 more developed regions 1237 1275 930 1100 75 86 less developed regions 5671 7875 2556 5186 45 66 least developed regions 855 1673 249 914 29 55 Which relationship can be confirmed from the table?

options.A: The least developed regions have the largest urban populations, actual or predicted, in both years.
options.B: The more developed regions have the lowest growth rate of urbanisation between 2010 and 2050.
options.C: The type of region with the greatest total population in 2010 is predicted to have the greatest rate of population growth by 2050.
options.D: The type of region with the greatest urban population in 2010 is predicted to have the highest level of urbanisation by 2050.

questions.questionText: In 2015, the World Bank agreed to give a loan of $650m to Angola to help stabilise the economy. The Bank said Angola needed to have a fiscal policy that would encourage the diversification of its economy. Which policy would be consistent with this requirement?

options.A: the lowering of interest rates to encourage investment in solar power
options.B: the relaxing of regulations to allow the development of a new hydro-power project
options.C: the spending of the loan supporting its oil industry after oil prices collapsed
options.D: the subsidising of a partnership with a French company to establish a chain of tourist hotels

questions.questionText: A country with demand-pull inflation decides to fix its exchange rates against other currencies above the purchasing power parities. What is likely to happen to the macroeconomic indicators shown? current account interest rate inflation rate balance

options.A: decrease decrease improve
options.B: decrease increase worsen
options.C: increase decrease worsen

questions.questionText: In the short run, which policy measure would tend to reduce a country’s balance of payments deficit but increase its inflation rate?

options.A: a decrease in the level of import tariffs
options.B: an appreciation of the country’s currency
options.C: an increase in the level of indirect taxes

questions.questionText: In an economy with unemployed resources the government increases its expenditure. When would this be least likely to increase national income by the full multiplier effect?

options.A: when the level of autonomous private investment is increased
options.B: when the marginal propensity to save is reduced
options.C: when the government allows money supply to expand
options.D: when the level of interest rates rises reasonable effort has been made by the publisher (UCLES) to trace copyright holders, but if any items requiring clearance have unwittingly been included, the publisher will be pleased to make amends at the earliest possible opportunity.
